questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about mechanical waves is INCORRECT?
options: Transverse waves can travel through solids and on the surface of liquids.
Longitudinal waves can travel through solids, liquids, and gases.
In a transverse wave, the particle displacement is parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
Sound waves in air are longitudinal waves.
questions.explanation: In a transverse wave, particle displacement is perpendicular to the direction of propagation. Parallel displacement defines a longitudinal wave.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The equation of a progressive wave is given by y(x, t) = 0.05 sin(20πt - 4πx), where x, y are in meters and t is in seconds. The velocity of the wave is:
questions.explanation: Velocity v = coefficient of t / coefficient of x = (20π)/(4π) = 5 m/s. The sign (ωt - kx) indicates positive x-direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Observe the snapshot of a transverse wave traveling to the right (positive x-direction) at a specific instant t. What is the direction of the instantaneous velocity of the particle at point P?
questions.explanation: Particle velocity v_p = -v_wave * slope. At P (downward slope of crest), slope is negative. v_wave is positive. v_p = -(+)(-) = Positive (Upward).
questions.imagePrompt: Image Prompt: A sine wave graph. A point P is marked on the curve between a peak and the following zero-crossing (the downward slope). An arrow indicates wave motion to the right.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform rope of length L and mass M hangs vertically from a rigid support. A transverse pulse is generated at the lower end. The time taken by the pulse to reach the top support is:
questions.explanation: Wave speed at height y is v = √(gy). Time t = ∫ dy/v from 0 to L. t = ∫ y^(-1/2) / √g dy = 2√(L/g).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two waves are represented by y1 = a sin(ωt - kx) and y2 = a cos(ωt - kx). The phase difference between them is:
questions.explanation: Convert cosine to sine: cos(θ) = sin(θ + π/2). The phase difference is π/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two wave pulses of identical shape but inverted amplitude are traveling towards each other on a string. At the exact moment they completely overlap, the shape of the string will be:
options: Two smaller pulses moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: By the principle of superposition, y_net = y1 + y2. Since y2 = -y1 (inverted), the sum is zero everywhere at the moment of overlap.
questions.imagePrompt: Image Prompt: Two triangular pulses on a string approaching each other. Pulse on left is upright, pulse on right is inverted.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A traveling wave passes from a heavier string (density μ2) to a lighter string (density μ1), where μ2 > μ1. Which of the following is true regarding the reflected and transmitted waves?
options: The reflected wave undergoes a phase change of π.
The reflected wave undergoes zero phase change.
The transmitted wave travels slower than the incident wave.
The transmitted wave undergoes a phase change of π.
questions.explanation: Reflection from a rarer medium (lighter string acts like a free end relative to heavier string) results in zero phase change. Transmitted waves never undergo phase inversion. Speed increases in lighter string.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two tuning forks A and B produce 4 beats per second. The frequency of A is 256 Hz. When a small piece of wax is attached to B, the beat frequency increases to 6 beats per second. What was the original frequency of B?
questions.explanation: Initial gap is 4. Wax lowers B's frequency. If B was 260, lowering it would reduce the gap towards 0 first. If B was 252, lowering it increases the gap to 6. Thus B was 252 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string is V. If the tension in the string is increased by 44% while keeping the linear mass density constant, the new speed will be:
questions.explanation: v is proportional to √T. T becomes 1.44T. New v = √(1.44) * v = 1.2v.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The diagram below shows the displacement-time graph of a particle in a medium under the influence of two sound waves of slightly different frequencies. Based on the graph, the beat frequency is:
questions.explanation: The graph shows amplitude waxing and waning. The time interval between two maxima (period of beats) is 0.5s. f_beat = 1/0.5 = 2 Hz.
questions.imagePrompt: Image Prompt: A beat pattern graph (Amplitude vs Time). The envelope shows maxima at t=0, t=0.5, t=1.0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The equation of a wave is y = 3 sin π(0.5x - 50t), where x is in cm and t is in seconds. The ratio of the maximum particle velocity to the wave velocity is:
questions.explanation: y = 3 sin(0.5πx - 50πt). Wave vel V = ω/k = 100. Particle max vel vp = Aω = 150π. Ratio = 1.5π.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two waves of intensities I and 4I interfere at a point. The maximum and minimum intensities produced are respectively:
questions.explanation: Max intensity = (√I + √4I)^2 = (3√I)^2 = 9I. Min intensity = (√I - √4I)^2 = (-√I)^2 = I.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A source of sound of frequency 600 Hz is placed inside water. The frequency of sound recorded by an observer standing in the air is:
questions.explanation: Frequency depends only on the source and does not change during refraction/transmission across media.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Refer to the graph showing the variation of pressure (P) with position (x) for a longitudinal wave. At which point is the displacement of the medium particles zero?
options: At all points A, B, and C
questions.explanation: Pressure nodes (B) correspond to Displacement antinodes (max displacement). Pressure antinodes (max compression A / rarefaction C) correspond to Displacement nodes (zero displacement).
questions.imagePrompt: Image Prompt: A cosine graph representing Pressure vs Position. A is a peak, B is zero-crossing, C is a trough.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wave pulse is described by y(x,t) = 10 / (2 + (x - 5t)^2). Which of the following statements is true?
options: The pulse travels in the negative x-direction.
The amplitude of the pulse is 10 units.
The pulse is symmetric and travels with speed 5 units.
This equation describes a standing wave.
questions.explanation: Form f(x-vt) implies positive direction. Speed v=5. Max value (Amplitude) occurs when denominator is min (i.e., 2), so Amplitude = 10/2 = 5.

questions.question: PASSAGE: If the power of the incident wave is Pi, what fraction of the power is reflected (Pr/Pi)?
questions.explanation: Since incident and reflected waves are in the same medium, Power is proportional to Amplitude squared. Ratio = (Ar/Ai)^2 = (1/3)^2 = 1/9.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two strings A and B made of same material are stretched by the same tension. Radius of A is double of B. The ratio vA/vB is:
questions.explanation: v ∝ 1/√μ ∝ 1/r. Since rA = 2rB, vA = vB/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: 56 tuning forks are arranged in a series such that each produces 4 beats/sec with the preceding one. The frequency of the last is three times the first. Frequency of the first is:
questions.explanation: f_last = f_first + (N-1)*beats. 3f = f + 55*4. 2f = 220. f = 110 Hz.
